title: Planner: private tasks stored in your private plan instead of Microsoft To Do
summary: The briefing accurately reports Microsoft's planned storage change, automatic deployment and December rollout window. The Teams admin path and PowerShell control are documented, and the page correctly distinguishes them from a switch to preserve To Do storage.

claims.claim: The change covers private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences.
claims.quote: Private tasks created in Planner and Planner-powered experiences are stored in the user’s private plan

claims.claim: The private plan provides a single place for tasks visible only to their owner.

claims.claim: No price, meter or license specific to this storage change is yet published.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private tasks private plan license pricing additional cost. Read licensing in manage-planner-app, Planner for admins and the Planner service description; none names a price, meter or license specific to this private-task storage change.

claims.claim: Learn says the Planner app in Teams displays Private Tasks under My Tasks.
claims.quote:
My Tasks: This view includes:
- Private Tasks: A dedicated place for the user to quickly create tasks in a default place.

claims.claim: Learn does not yet describe how the new storage change appears in the Teams app.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner Teams private tasks private plan new storage experience December 2026. Read manage-planner-app and Planner for admins; they describe the existing views but do not describe the new storage change's Teams presentation.

claims.where: controls[0].ui and controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions; rationale: risk
claims.claim: No admin UI or API switch is documented to keep new Planner private tasks in To Do instead of the private Planner plan.
claims.quote: Searched: "Planner" "private tasks" "opt" "storage"; "Planner" "private tasks" "Set-PlannerConfiguration"; private-plan Graph query. Read manage-planner-app, disable-planner and Graph Planner overviews; found general availability controls, not a storage-choice switch.

claims.claim: Teams admin center > Teams apps > Manage apps > Planner > Block turns off the Planner app for the organisation in Teams.
claims.quote:
In the left pane of the Teams admin center, go to Teams apps > Manage apps.
To turn off Planner for your organization, search for the Planner app, select it, and then select Block.

claims.claim: Update-M365TeamsApp -Id <app-id> -IsBlocked <Boolean> sets the Teams app's tenant state.
claims.quote:
This cmdlet updates app state and app available values for the Microsoft Teams app.
-Id <String>
[-IsBlocked <Boolean>]
-Id: Application ID of Microsoft Teams app.
-IsBlocked: The state of the app in the tenant.

claims.claim: The cmdlet reference describes examples using -IsBlocked $true as unblocking an app.
claims.quote:
PS C:\> Update-M365TeamsApp -Id 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b -IsBlocked $true

Unblocks Bookings app (App ID 4c4ec2e8-4a2c-4bce-8d8f-00fc664a4e5b).

claims.claim: The Teams app control governs Planner availability in Teams, not whether new private tasks remain in To Do.
claims.quote: You can turn off or turn on the app at the org level on the Manage apps page in the Teams admin center.

claims.claim: The cited Planner licensing pages do not name a separate license for private tasks.
claims.quote: Searched: Planner private tasks private plan license pricing additional cost. Read the licensing section of manage-planner-app and the full Planner for admins page; they specify product and premium entitlements, not a separate private-task license.

claims.claim: Other clouds are not listed on the roadmap item, without that establishing their exclusion.
claims.quote: "clouds": ["Worldwide (Standard Multi-Tenant)"]
